findings.text: The fall-through past an absent raw file keys on 'no non-blank line' (_holds_a_record_line), not on 'no parseable row', so a raw file whose only content is an unparseable (but non-blank) line is still selected, the read raises, and the minute tier that holds the rows is never read -- the opposite of the retention block's settled reading (line 576: 'A raw file with no parseable row does not stop the fall-through, so the index reads that job's minute tier') and of the antecedent review's own framing of this boundary ('the implementation must decide tier by whether the file actually yields rows'). _raw_has_no_row returns True only when the file cannot be opened (OSError) or holds no non-blank line; a truncated or corrupt record line is not blank, so the file is offered and _parse refuses it in place. The node documents this choice deliberately ('the fall-through is for an absent tier, not for corrupt data'), and the plan's first sentence ('empty or unreadable ... counts as absent') admits the narrower reading -- corrupt content is neither empty nor unopenable -- so this is a genuine ambiguity, not a plain miss; but the plan's second sentence names exactly this case and the fix does not cover it, and the reviewed run's own new test pins the narrower behaviour by asserting the read raises. Reproduced at the reviewed head (probe-corrupt.log): with a valid minute and hour tier beside a raw file whose only line is a truncated JSON record, one tick raises ValueError 'invalid record JSON', the job's held tiers are set() and its token totals are None/None/None, while the minute tier (which holds 2000/1000/800) was never read. No test covers the unparseable-line fall-through; the empty-raw test uses raw.write_text(""), i.e. zero bytes.

item_verdicts.call_sites: verified the two production call sites of index.ingest that offer a directory -- imas_ambix/agent/watch.py:920 and imas_ambix/agent/watch.py:1020 -- both pass discover(directory), the whole directory; telemetry_ingest.tick hands index.ingest the whole discovered set (telemetry_ingest.py:190). The fall-through therefore sees every tier a job offers, and the selection can move a job from raw to minute.
item_verdicts.diff: Read commits 3d14085c (implementation) and e7fa17da (evidence fragment) against base 1c871e0f. 3d14085c: four files, +161/-25 -- imas_ambix/agent/telemetry_index.py (+71), imas_ambix/agent/telemetry_ingest.py (+39/-25 line churn), tests/test_telemetry_index.py (+56), tests/test_telemetry_ingest.py (+20/-4). e7fa17da: docs/evidence/fragments/serving-record-warehouse/srw-index-tier-choice-survives-empty-and-failed-reads.html (+97). Both commits carry a conventional subject and a body; neither carries an AI trailer; no plan, sprint or ticket identifier appears in either message or in the changed source.
item_verdicts.done_when: The node's done-when (as dispatched) asks that a raw file with no parseable row be treated as absent, that the deselected-tier drop happen only after the selected tier is read 'in the same transaction', that DEFAULT_CADENCE_SECONDS be 60.0, and that the named tests and gate pass. The gate passes (95 passed, guard not in this run's declared set, ruff clean per the reviewed run's own logs; this review re-ran the five-file gate green at both arms). The empty-raw and failed-read tests exist and pass; the 60 s default test exists and passes. The done-when's literal wording 'no parseable row' is only partly met -- the implementation's predicate is 'no non-blank line', which diverges for an unparseable line (the finding). The 'in the same transaction' clause is met in guarantee but not in mechanism: the drop is a separate transaction ordered after the read's commit, not folded into it; the observable guarantee the clause exists to give -- a read that raises leaves the samples in place -- holds, and the antecedent review that named this repair explicitly offered 'read first and drop after' as an equivalent local repair, so this is recorded as a satisfied deviation rather than a defect. The gate log's first line names the commit it ran at (3d14085c) and each command records EXIT=0/1; the evidence fragment ends with a trailing newline (verified).
item_verdicts.goal: The node's declared goal is to make the one-tier choice fall through past an empty raw file and never lose a job's samples to a failed read. Both limbs are implemented and verified: ingest drops from the offered set any raw file that _raw_has_no_row reports carries no record line (telemetry_index.py:913), so one_tier_per_job selects the finest tier that holds rows and the job is read from its minute (then hour) tier; and _drop_deselected_tiers(chosen) now runs after the read loop and its commit (telemetry_index.py:1007), so a read that raises on the selected file leaves the previously held samples in place. The declared empty-raw behaviour is asserted and passes (test_a_job_whose_raw_file_is_empty_is_answered_from_its_minute_tier: totals 2000/1000/800, held tier {minute}). The cadence limb also holds: DEFAULT_CADENCE_SECONDS is 60.0 and the module and entry point describe the standing loop the fleet supervisor runs, matching the plan's locked ingest-cadence decision (plan line 747-755: every 60 s under the fleet supervisor). Goal fidelity loses points only for the unparseable-line boundary the plan's reading 10 names and the fix does not cover -- see the finding.
